newInput: How do you handle merge conflicts in Git?

answersA.title: Handling Git merge conflicts
answersA.text: When merge conflicts occur in Git, it means that Git cannot automatically reconcile changes made to the same part of a file in different branches. To handle them, you first need to identify the conflicting files, which Git marks clearly. You then manually edit these files to resolve the discrepancies, choosing which changes to keep or how to combine them. After resolving the conflicts, you stage the modified files using `git add` and then commit the merge.

After resolving all conflicts, you stage the modified files using `git add` and commit the merge with `git commit`.

newInput: Explain the CAP theorem.

answersA.title: Explain the CAP theorem
answersA.text: The CAP theorem states that a distributed data store cannot simultaneously provide more than two out of the following three guarantees: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance. In practice, systems must choose which two to prioritize, as network partitions are inevitable. For example, a system might choose Consistency and Partition Tolerance (CP) by sacrificing some availability during a partition, or Availability and Partition Tolerance (AP) by allowing inconsistent reads.

For example, a system might choose to remain available by serving potentially stale data (AP), or it might prioritize consistency by refusing to serve data until the partition is resolved (CP).

answersA.text: Eventual consistency is a consistency model in distributed systems. It means that if no new updates are made to a given data item, eventually all accesses to that item will return the last updated value. answersA.text:
Debouncing a function is a technique to ensure that a function is only executed after a certain period of inactivity. This is commonly used for events that fire rapidly, like resizing a window or typing in a search bar, to prevent excessive function calls.

To implement debouncing, you typically use a timer. When the debounced function is called, you clear any existing timer and set a new one. The original function is only executed if the timer completes without being cleared, meaning no new calls have occurred within the specified delay.

answersA.text: Computed properties in Vue.js are functions that Vue caches based on their reactive dependencies. When these dependencies change, Vue re-evaluates the computed property. This is useful for deriving data that depends on other data in your Vue instance, ensuring that the derived data is always up-to-date and efficiently calculated only when necessary. They are accessed like regular properties, not called as functions.

answersA.title: Mutex vs. Semaphore
answersA.text: A mutex is a locking mechanism used to ensure that only one thread can access a shared resource at a time. It's like a key to a room; only the thread holding the key can enter. A semaphore, on the other hand, is a signaling mechanism that controls access to a pool of resources. It maintains a counter; threads can access a resource if the counter is greater than zero, and the counter is decremented. When a thread releases a resource, the counter is incremented.

answersA.title: Qu'est-ce que le TDD ?
answersA.text: Le TDD, ou Test-Driven Development, est une méthodologie de développement logiciel. Elle consiste à écrire les tests unitaires avant de coder la fonctionnalité elle-même. Le cycle typique est : écrire un test qui échoue, écrire le code nécessaire pour que le test passe, puis refactoriser le code. Cela permet d'obtenir un code plus propre, mieux conçu et avec une couverture de tests plus élevée.

answersA.title: Qu'est-ce que le TDD ?

answersC.title: Qu'est-ce que le TDD ?

newInput: Quelle est la différence entre une file et une pile ?

answersA.title: Difference between queue and stack
answersA.text:
Une file d'attente est une structure de données qui suit le principe "premier entré, premier sorti" (FIFO). Imaginez une file d'attente à la caisse : la première personne arrivée est la première servie. Les opérations principales sont l'ajout d'un élément à la fin (enqueue) et la suppression d'un élément du début (dequeue).

Une pile, quant à elle, suit le principe "dernier entré, premier sorti" (LIFO). Pensez à une pile d'assiettes : vous retirez l'assiette du dessus, qui est la dernière que vous avez posée. Les opérations clés sont l'ajout d'un élément au sommet (push) et la suppression d'un élément du sommet (pop).

answersA.title: Différence entre file et pile
answersA.text: Une file d'attente est une structure de données qui suit le principe du premier entré, premier sorti (FIFO). Les éléments sont ajoutés à l'arrière (enqueue) et retirés de l'avant (dequeue). Une pile, quant à elle, suit le principe du dernier entré, premier sorti (LIFO). Les éléments sont ajoutés et retirés du sommet (push et pop).
